author.name: Richard Dawkins
author.heading: About Richard Dawkins
author.bio: Richard Dawkins is an evolutionary biologist whose books connect genetics with questions about human life and culture. He held Oxford’s professorship for the public understanding of science from 1995 to 2008; in Unweaving the Rainbow he argues that scientific explanations can deepen wonder.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Dawkins sets the certainty of death beside the much greater number of possible people who will never exist. That reversal introduces a chapter about how familiarity can dull a person’s appreciation of being alive, within a book defending science as a source of wonder.
